Icon sizes

The same icons at smaller sizes. At 40px and below, parts marked as detail are hidden so the shape still reads.

Drawing rules

The skill would follow these rules for every new device.

Real models
Every drawing is named after a real device and follows its layout, colors and, in Device view, its real size.
Photo check
Before a drawing is final, it is placed next to a front photo of the real model. Part positions are measured from the photo in millimetres, and any part that is missing, misplaced or the wrong color is fixed. Each card links its photo.
Two views
Icon: 64 × 64 units with the essential parts. Device: the full drawing, where one unit is one millimetre.
Scale
Set --u to choose how many pixels one unit is. Highlights and shadows grow with the drawing through --e.
Curves
Real devices rarely have straight edges. Outlines, panels and keys are drawn as rounded shapes whose edges bow outward slightly, traced from the photo.
Grouping
Parts moulded as one piece are drawn as one unit divided by thin seams, like each N-Gage keypad row and its paired soft keys. Parts that stand alone get their own outline and shadow.
Light
Light comes from above. Highlight, base and shadow tones come from one --body color through color-mix().
Materials
Shaded plastic, leatherette, chrome, knurled dials, lens glass, LCD, CRT tube and tinted cassette windows.
Detail level
Icon parts with the class .d are hidden at 40px and below.
Motion
Each device does what the real one did. Screens show the real interface at the real pixel resolution, scaled up with hard pixel edges: 84×48 on the 3310, 160×144 on the Game Boy, 128×128 on the 3200, 176×208 on the N-Gage. Key presses match what appears on screen.
Logos
Wordmarks are drawn as plain text set close to the original, on every device whose front carries one (the Leica M3 has none on its front). Brand names are trademarks of their owners; check you have the right to use them in a product.
Hover, focus or tap a card to see its motion. Each drawing was checked against the reference photo linked on its card. Photos are from Wikimedia Commons, CRT Database and Teenage Engineering. Sizes marked approx. are estimates.
